title: The Golden Horde Rides
tagline: From Mongolia to Poland — the unstoppable cavalry of the steppes.

scenes.text: 1236. Batu Khan, grandson of Genghis, leads the largest mounted army in history westward. The Mongol Empire will touch Europe.
Rus principalities fall one by one — Vladimir, Kiev, Ryazan. The Mongol cavalry moves faster than any army before it.

challenge.instruction: Ryazan is the first city in Batu's path. Close the ring round its walls so the prince cannot break out before the city falls.
challenge.fact: Batu Khan (c.1207–1255) was the grandson of Genghis Khan and founder of the Golden Horde. In 1241, he led the most western Mongol campaign in history, crushing Polish and Hungarian armies simultaneously and reaching the gates of Vienna — before news of Ögedei Khan's death caused the army to withdraw.

params.title: The Ring Round Ryazan, 1237
params.intro: You command the black attackers closing on Ryazan. Keep Prince Yuri from every corner until the moves run out — or surround him for an early win. The edge counts against him.
params.fact: In December 1237 the Mongols ringed Ryazan with a palisade so no one could get in or out, battered the walls with siege engines for five days and stormed the city on 21 December. Prince Yuri Igorevich died with his people; Vladimir fell the following February.

scenes.text: Poland and Hungary are shattered at the battles of Legnica and Mohi. Western Europe trembles. Then — a miracle for Europe — Ögedei Khan dies. Batu turns back.

challenge.instruction: Batu's northern wing in Poland and his own army in Hungary must strike within days of each other. Bend the signal through the mirrors so both armies move on the same plan.
challenge.fact: In April 1241 two Mongol forces about 600 km apart won within two days of each other: Baidar and Kadan's wing crushed Duke Henry II of Silesia at Legnica on 9 April, and Batu and Subutai destroyed King Béla IV's Hungarian army at Mohi on 11 April. The Mongols withdrew not because of military defeat but because Ögedei Khan's death required the princes to return east.

scenes.text: Batu founds the Golden Horde on the Volga steppes — a Mongol khanate that will rule Russia for 200 years. He rules from his golden tent, dispensing justice and tribute.

challenge.instruction: From his golden tent at Sarai, Batu taxes every caravan that crosses the western steppe. Buy up the caravanserais and outgrow the rival houses before the season ends.
challenge.fact: Batu founded Sarai on the lower Volga as the Golden Horde's capital. It sat on the northern branch of the Silk Road, where caravans carried furs, slaves, silk and silver between the Rus lands, Central Asia and the Black Sea — and the Horde took its tolls on all of it. The Franciscan William of Rubruck, who visited Batu's camp in 1253, described a moving city of tents and wagons.

scenes.text: He hosts Persian ambassadors, Chinese envoys, and European monks — a cosmopolitan court on horseback.

challenge.instruction: Mongol warriors trained for war through the nerge — a great ring drawn across the steppe. Post your riders to close every gap before the wild horses break out. The same maneuver will encircle armies.
challenge.fact: The nerge was sport and military training at once. Thousands of horsemen spread across the steppe and slowly tightened the ring, and generals studied its coordination problems — timing, signalling over distance, closing both flanks together — then used the same solutions in battle.

scenes.text: The Golden Horde reshapes Eurasian trade and politics for generations. Batu Khan: conqueror, founder, statesman of the steppe.

challenge.instruction: The European knights cannot resist chasing a fleeing enemy. Let them ride into the trap, then close the ring with one decisive move.
challenge.fact: The feigned retreat was the signature Mongol tactic in Europe. Heavy knights, trained to charge and pursue, could not resist a retreating enemy. The Mongols would fall back for miles, drawing the pursuers into scattered disorder, then wheel and destroy them in detail. European commanders had no answer for an 'enemy' that ran away only to fight on its own terms.

challenge.instruction: The Horde rules from the Volga to Kiev because the khan's word travels fast. Carry his order through every town and back to Sarai, changing horses at the yam stations.
challenge.fact: The Golden Horde that Batu established dominated the Russian steppe for 250 years, collecting tribute from every Russian principality. Moscow grew wealthy as a tax collector for the Horde — a relationship that profoundly shaped Russian political culture, centralizing power and accustoming rulers to absolute authority.

scenes.speaker: Batu Khan
scenes.text: Taira no Tadanori waits at Changan, but nothing is happening there, and without an event there is no fight. I will go first; the turn after I arrive, play the Battlefield card on Changan and we attack.

challenge.instruction: Fight lesson 3 · Starting an Event. Deploy Batu Khan to Changan and End Turn. Next turn play the Battlefield card there, add your follower and win one attack.
challenge.fact: Event cards start a scenario at a location where you already have a Great Person, and only one who arrived on an earlier turn can start it. A local event keeps running until a player ends it.
